id: 第一章-人性篇-竹林中-多襄丸答捕吏的供词-p1

en: 第一章-人性篇-竹林中-多襄丸答捕吏的供词
I did kill that man, but I absolutely did not kill the woman.
u.src: 我的确杀了那个男人，但我绝对没杀那女人。
至于她的去向？
鬼才知道。
啊，别急。

en: No matter how much you torture me, I do not know what I do not know!
u.src: 再怎么拷问我，不知道就是不知道啊！

en: And since I have already been caught, there is no need for me to hide anything anymore.
u.src: 而且我既然已经被抓住了，我也没必要掩藏什么了。

en: Yesterday at noon, I ran into the couple on the road.
u.src: 昨儿中午，我在路上遇见他们夫妻。

en: Just then, a gust of wind lifted the woman's veil, and I saw her face.
u.src: 当时刚好来了一阵风吹起了女人的面纱，我看见她的脸。

en: But it lasted only an instant, and then it was gone.
u.src: 但也就一刹那，就消失了。

en: Perhaps that was why I was drawn to the woman's beauty.
u.src: 可能是这个原因吧，我被这女人的美貌吸引。

en: On a sudden impulse, I decided to kill the man and take the woman for myself.
u.src: 我临时起意，决定杀了男的，霸占女的。

en: Hmph, killing a man is no great difficulty for me.
u.src: 咳，杀一个男人，对我来说没什么难度。

en: To take possession of that woman, I first had to kill that man.
u.src: 要霸占那女人，必要先杀了那男人。

en: The only difference is that I kill with a sword, while you kill with money, power, and false lies.
u.src: 只不过我杀人用的是刀，你们杀人用金钱、权势、虚伪的谎言。

en: True, when you kill, no blood is seen, and the body still lives, but the person is certainly dead.
u.src: 的确，你们杀人不见血，肉体还活着——但人确实是死了。

en: That sin must reach far deeper, must it not!
u.src: 这罪孽要更深远吧！

en: I wonder which of us is truly the worse one?
u.src: 也不知道咱们谁更坏一些呢？

en: He shows a mocking smile on his face.
u.src: （面露讥讽的笑容）

en: Of course, if I could have taken the woman without killing the man, that would have been best.
u.src: 当然了，要是不用杀男人就能霸占女人，也挺好的。

en: Yes, at the time I had also thought about a way to carry off the woman without killing the man.
u.src: 对了，当时我也想过不杀男人也能抢走女人的办法。

en: But on that road through Yamashina, there was no good way to do it,
u.src: 不过在那山科的驿路上面，没什么好办法，

en: so I deliberately tricked them into going into the mountains.
u.src: 因此我才设计骗他们进山的。

en: This was no trouble at all.
u.src: 这毫无难度。

en: I struck up a friendly conversation with the couple and deceived them by saying,
u.src: 我跟那对夫妻套近乎，骗他们说，

en: that an ancient tomb had been found on the mountain opposite,
u.src: 对面山上发现个古墓，

en: that I had dug up many long swords and mirrors there,
u.src: 我在那挖出许多大刀和镜子，

en: and had secretly buried them in the bamboo grove behind the mountain.
u.src: 偷偷埋在山后的竹林里了。

en: If anyone wanted to buy them, I would sell them for money.
u.src: 要是有人想买，给钱就卖。

en: That man had his heart stirred by my lie.
u.src: ——那个男人被我的谎言撬动了心。

en: Just look how hateful greed can be!
u.src: ——你瞅瞅，贪恋多可恶啊！

en: In less than half an hour, the husband and wife followed me into the mountain.
u.src: 也就不到半小时，他们夫妻就跟我进了山。

en: When we reached the front of the bamboo grove, I tricked them by saying the treasure was buried right here.
u.src: 到了竹林前面，我就骗他们说宝贝就在这里埋着呢。

en: The man was greedy for a small gain, so of course he was eager to go in.
u.src: 男的贪图小利，当然着急进去。

en: But the woman never got down from her horse at all and insisted on waiting outside.
u.src: 但是那个女人根本没下马，坚持在外面等着。

en: I suppose she said that because she saw how dense the shrubs were in the bamboo grove.
u.src: 我估计她是看竹林灌木密集，才会这么说。

en: To tell the truth, that suited me perfectly, so I left the woman outside and went into the bamboo grove with the man.
u.src: 说真的，这正中我下怀，把女人留在外面，我跟那男人一起进了竹林。

en: The outer edge of the bamboo grove was all pillars, and only after going in a little more than half a cho did I see a sparse stand of cedars.
u.src: 竹林外围都是柱子，进到约莫半町多的地方，才看到一片稀稀拉拉的杉树。

en: This was exactly the right place for me to carry out my plan.
u.src: ——这正是我实施计划的好地方。

en: I pushed aside the bamboo branches and lied with a perfectly serious air, saying that the treasure was buried under the cedar trees.
u.src: 我扒开竹枝，若有其事的撒谎，说宝贝就在杉树下面埋着呢。

en: No sooner had I said it than the man hurried off toward the low cedars deep in the bamboo grove.
u.src: 我刚说完，男的拔腿就往竹林深处的矮小杉树走去。

en: There were not many bamboos there, and several cedars stood side by side; catching him off guard, I knocked the man down.
u.src: 那里竹子不多，并排长着几颗杉树——我猝不及防按倒了那个男人。

en: The man seemed very strong, just as one would expect of a sword-bearing warrior.
u.src: 那人力气似乎很大，不愧是带刀武士。

en: But because I had taken him completely by surprise, there was nothing he could do.
u.src: 不过我打他个措手不及，他也是无可奈何。

en: I tied him up at the foot of one of the cedar trees.
u.src: 我把他捆在一颗杉树脚下。
至于绳子啊？

en: In the thieving trade, you never know when you may have to climb over a wall and break into a house, so I always kept it tucked at my waist.
u.src: 做贼的行当，保不齐什么时候就翻墙入室，我随时都别在腰间的。

ja: きないようにするためだ。
en: Yes, I stuffed bamboo leaves into his mouth so that his shouting would not bring trouble.
u.src: 是的，我用竹叶堵住了他的嘴，免得他喊叫惹来麻烦。

en: After I had dealt with the man, I went out and told the woman that her husband seemed to have fallen suddenly ill and that she should hurry and look at him.
u.src: 我收拾好了男人，就出去跟女人说，她丈夫似乎的了急症，让她快去瞅瞅。

en: Of course, she fell for it too.
u.src: 当然了，她也上当了。

en: The woman took off her veiled ichimegasa hat, and I took her by the hand and lured her deep into the bamboo grove.
u.src: 女人摘掉了带着面纱的市女笠，我拉着她的手把她骗进竹林深处。

en: As soon as the woman saw her husband tied at the foot of a cedar, before I knew it, she had drawn a gleaming little knife from inside her robe, already out of its sheath.
u.src: 女人一看他丈夫被捆在杉树脚上——不知何时，她从怀里掏出一把闪亮的小刀，刀已出鞘。

en: It was the first time I had ever seen such a fierce woman.
u.src: 我还是头一次见这么厉害的女人！

en: At that moment, if I had been careless for even an instant, she would have stabbed me in the belly with one thrust.
u.src: 那时候我只要一不小心，就会被她一刀捅进肚皮。

en: No, even if I had dodged that one thrust, with her slashing wildly, I truly cannot say what wounds I might have suffered.
u.src: 没有，就算逃过了这一刀，她乱刀挥舞，我真不好说会受什么伤呢。

en: But I am Tajomaru, after all; without even using my long sword, I knocked her little knife to the ground.
u.src: 不过我是多襄丸啊，大刀都没使，就把她的小刀打落在地。

en: No matter how formidable a woman may be, without a weapon she can do nothing.
u.src: 再怎么厉害的女人，没有武器也无可奈何了。

en: Just as I had planned, I forced myself on the woman without killing the man.
u.src: 按照原计划，我在不杀害男人的前提下，霸占了这女人。

en: Not kill the man, of course; as long as I could take possession of the woman, I had no intention of killing him.
u.src: 不杀了男人——当然，只要能霸占这女人，我没想着要杀了他。

en: But just as I was about to leave the woman lying on the ground in pain and flee out of the bamboo grove, she suddenly grabbed my arm like a madwoman.
u.src: 然而当我准备扔下趴在地上痛苦的女人往竹林外逃窜的时候，那个女人突然疯狂的抓住了我的胳膊。

en: Sobbing, she cried out, Whether it is you or my husband, one of you two has to die.
u.src: 她抽抽噎噎的喊道，“你也好，我丈夫也好，你们俩必须得死一个。

en: After being shamed before two men, I would rather die than live.
u.src: 在两个男人眼前出丑，我生不如死。”

en: At last, gasping for breath, she said, Whichever one of you survives, I will go with him.
u.src: 最后她有气喘吁吁的说了句，“你们两个中间，谁活下来，我就跟谁。”

en: Only then did I suddenly want to kill that man.
u.src: 这个时候我才突然想杀死那个男人的。
（阴险狠毒的亢奋）

en: Hearing me say this, you must surely think I am more cruel than you are.
u.src: 听我这么说，你们一定觉得我比你们残忍。

en: That is because you did not see that woman’s face, especially her two eyes blazing like fire.
u.src: 那是因为你们没看见那个女人的脸，尤其是她那双如烈火般的双眸。

en: When my gaze met hers, I secretly resolved in my heart that even if the heavens struck me down, I would take her as my wife.
u.src: 我的眼神和她的眼神对视的时候，我心里暗暗决定，就算五雷轰顶，我也要把她娶回家。

en: I had only one thought: to marry her.
u.src: 我只有娶了她这一个想法。

en: This was not the shameless, vile lust you are imagining.
u.src: 这不是你们臆想的那种无耻卑劣的色欲。

en: If at that moment I had had no thought beyond lust, I would have kicked that woman down and fled at once.
u.src: 如果我当时除了色欲之外没有别的想法，我就是踢到这个女人，赶紧逃走。

en: If that had been the case, I would not have killed this man either.
u.src: 如果是这样的话，我也就不会杀了这男人了。

en: But in the gloomy bamboo grove, I studied the woman’s face closely.
u.src: 但是我在沉郁的竹林中认真观察了女人的脸。

en: At that moment I decided that before leaving, I had to kill this man.
u.src: 那时候我就决定了，走之前，我必须杀死这个男人。

en: As for killing the man, I wanted to be fair about that too.
u.src: 至于杀男人嘛，我也想公平一点。

en: I untied his ropes and fought him in a duel.
u.src: 我给他松了绳子，跟他决斗。

en: The rope at the foot of the cedar was the one I forgot to take away and left behind then.
u.src: （杉树脚下的绳子，就是当时忘了带走扔掉的。）

en: The man turned deathly pale and immediately drew his sword.
u.src: 男人脸煞白，立刻大刀出鞘。

en: In an instant, he silently lunged at me.
u.src: 一瞬间，就沉默的扑向了我。

en: There is no need to say much about how it ended.
u.src: ——结果如何，不必多言。

en: After twenty-three exchanges, my sword pierced his chest.
u.src: 打到二十三个回合，我的大刀刺进了他的胸膛。

en: Remember this: it was the twenty-third exchange.
u.src: 记住——是第二十三个回合。

en: Even today, I still admire him greatly.
u.src: 到今天，我依然很佩服他。

en: Because he was the first man who could trade more than twenty exchanges with me.
u.src: 因为他是第一个能我交手二十个回合以上的人。
（开怀的笑）

en: After the man fell, I carried my blood-soaked sword and went to look for the woman.
u.src: 男人倒下之后，我提着沾满鲜血的大刀，去找女人。

en: To my surprise, the woman had already run away.
u.src: 没想到，女人已经跑掉了。

en: As for where she had run off to?
u.src: 至于她跑到哪里去了？

en: I searched all through that grove of cedars, but there was not the slightest trace of footprints on the bamboo leaves.
u.src: 我在那片杉树中找了个遍，但是竹叶上一点踩踏的痕迹也没有。

en: When I listened closely, all I could hear was the man breathing his last.
u.src: 仔细听了听，也只听见男子的断气声。

en: Most likely, that woman ran away just as I began the duel.
u.src: 很可能我刚开始决斗的时候，那个女人就跑掉了。

en: Thinking that might have happened, I took the long sword and the bow and arrows to save my own life, and went back the way I had come.
u.src: ——想到这种可能，我为了保命，就拿了大刀和弓箭，折返原路。

en: The woman's horse was quietly grazing by the roadside.
u.src: 女人的马在路边安静的吃草。

en: There is no need to speak any further about what happened after that.
u.src: 之后的事情就不用再提了。

en: As for the long sword, I had already sold it before entering the capital.
u.src: 至于大刀，进京之前我早就卖掉了。

en: That is all of my testimony.
u.src: ——我的供词就是这些。

en: Everyone must die sooner or later, so go ahead and kill me.
u.src: 人固有一死，杀了我吧。

en: With an air of righteous defiance.
u.src: （大义凌然的样子）
